                    ### Question
                    Which of the activity deficits in the following enzymes of the urea cycle can cause an orotic aciduria, in addition to hyperammonemia ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Ornithine transcarbamylase.
opb. Arginase.
opc. Arginine succinate synthase.
opd. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency is the only urea cycle disorder that leads to orotic aciduria in addition to hyperammonemia. This is because the deficiency causes an accumulation of carbamoyl phosphate, which then enters the pyrimidine synthesis pathway, leading to increased production of orotic acid and resulting in orotic aciduria. Arginase deficiency leads to hyperargininemia but does not have a direct link to orotic aciduria. Arginine succinate synthase deficiency results in citrullinemia, which also does not directly cause orotic aciduria. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase deficiency results in decreased carbamoyl phosphate, reducing the substrate for pyrimidine synthesis, making orotic aciduria unlikely. The retrieved evidence paths do not directly support or clarify the mechanisms of orotic aciduria in the context of these enzyme deficiencies and are therefore not incorporated into the final reasoning.
